stock.description: BlackJAX NUTS, window adaptation, target acceptance 0.8

arcsinh.description: NUTS on the calibrated coordinate-wise arcsinh pullback

tukey_h.description: Same pipeline and Phase 1, Tukey h-map x = mu + R z exp(h z^2 / 2); (R, h) by Tukey-h maximum likelihood, h = 0 unless a likelihood-ratio test (deflated by the effective sample size of the Phase 1 draws) rejects it

tukey_h0.description: tukey_h with the guard never rejecting (level 0): h = 0 on every coordinate

config.init: Uniform(-2.0, 2.0)^d per chain from numpy default_rng(seed), redrawn up to 100 times until the log density is finite; shared by all arms

notes: Every arm runs sample_blackjax_unified_nuts on Stan's unconstrained space via BridgeStan (propto, Jacobian).
ESS, R-hat and reference agreement are computed on the constrained parameters that have reference draws.
min_* ESS is the worst reference parameter; converged means max rank-normalised R-hat <= 1.01.

ref_*: agreement with posteriordb's reference draws; tail probabilities at the reference's 1/5/95/99% quantiles and means, z = (run - reference) / sqrt(MCSE_run^2 + MCSE_ref^2), averaged (abs) or maximal.
tail_alignment_* is the library's tail-alignment check on the sampled (unconstrained) draws.
tukey_h_n_positive counts unconstrained coordinates whose calibrated h is positive (the guard rejected h = 0).

tukey_h_ref_positive: the same guard on exact draws, as many reference draws as Phase 1 calibrates from (subsampled with the row's seed, unconstrained); null when the reference lacks a parameter of the model.
calib_*: Phase 1's location and scale against the run's own post-warm-up draws (unconstrained, scale = IQR / 1.349): max |mu - median| / scale and max of R / scale or scale / R. Null for stock.
Ratios are paired by seed (same initial positions and JAX key) and summarised by median and IQR.
wall_time_sec includes JAX compilation and the host callbacks; vectorised chains also evaluate the model for chains whose trajectory has ended. Do not quote it as an efficiency measure.
